record.notes: There are 12 national allocators plus the EuroHPC JU, and they are the only entries. The Finnish national route states a useful floor of 1 million core hours for a developer project, which is the clearest published size found for a LUMI national allocation. GPU-hour figures for LUMI-G are set per national allocator and are not published centrally, so the field is null rather than borrowed from the EuroHPC tables.

record.provider: LUMI-O (CSC / EuroHPC LUMI) — 150 TB allocated per LUMI project by default

free_tier.stated: 'LUMI-O offers a total of 30 PB storage space ... By default 150 TB of storage space is allocated per LUMI project, but projects can request for more LUMI-O storage space by contacting the LUMI helpdesk.' This is the single largest default per-project object-storage quota found in the entire survey.

egress.terms: Unmetered; public buckets and presigned URLs are served over HTTPS. 'It is possible to share public data across the internet (for the duration of your project)' and 'to set a temporary access link to otherwise private data'.

record.tooling: rclone, s3cmd, aws cli, LUMI web interface. Credentials are LUMI-O access tokens generated at auth.lumidata.eu, scoped to a project.
record.chaining: 150 TB × N LUMI projects. A LUMI project is the unit; Finnish researchers create LUMI projects through MyCSC (the 'LUMI' project category) and LUMI is also reachable through EuroHPC Benchmark/Regular access and through national shares (e.g. SURF's Small Compute applications include 'up to 100,000 TB-hours project space storage' on LUMI). Every LUMI project carries LUMI-O by default: 'All LUMI projects have LUMI-O available by default.'
record.limits_note: Per-object-cap: 500,000 objects per bucket, same as Allas. No per-object byte cap documented. Retention is the project lifetime, explicitly: 'Data lifetime in LUMI-O is the same as your project lifetime.' request-rate: not published. Note: 'In LUMI-O one project is treated as one account: all project members have the same access/user rights'. So quota is per project, never per person.

identity_cost.detail: inferred from the category 'academic'; the source record states no identity cost, so this is a class assumption, not evidence

record.reliability_note: Data dies with the project; no backup is implied and objects cannot be modified in place.
